title: Doubly Linked Lists
summary: Extends singly linked lists two ways: circular lists connect the tail back to the head (good for round-robin and repeat playlists), and doubly linked lists give each node a prev pointer as well as next, so you can move backward (good for undo/redo and browser history). Step-by-step guide arrives when the lecture is published.
goal: Build a doubly linked list that can walk both directions, and choose between singly, circular and doubly linked lists.

steps.title: Read the lesson
steps.detail: Read the Doubly & Circular Linked Lists page, including the 'Conventional Uses' table.
steps.doneWhen: You can name one use case for each of the three list types.

steps.title: Run a doubly linked list backward
steps.detail: This uses the lesson's DNode and add_node, plus a short backward walk from the tail.

steps.title: Understand the circular loop check
steps.detail: In the lesson's circular add_node, the loop is while current.next != self.head instead of while current.next. Explain to yourself why the normal check would loop forever.
steps.doneWhen: You can say why a circular list never reaches None.

steps.title: Talk through Browser History
steps.detail: One assignment is a Browser History program with a doubly linked list. Before coding, describe visit, back and forward in plain English and give each one's Big-O (moving back or forward one step is O(1)).
steps.doneWhen: You can explain the design and Big-O out loud.

concepts.meaning: Each node points both to the next node and the previous one.
The link back to the node before this one.
The last node points back to the head, forming a loop.
The last node in the list.
Taking turns in a repeating cycle, like a playlist on repeat.
